attempts.summary: Joined node1/node2/node3 into a single RabbitMQ 3.10.0 cluster (installed via official RabbitMQ+Erlang RPM repos), created the `payments` vhost, an `app_payments` application user (password generated on-node with openssl, stored only in /root/app_payments.pw) with full permissions on that vhost, and a durable quorum queue `orders` replicated across all 3 nodes. Verified durability by publishing 3 durable messages, stopping RabbitMQ on the leader node (node1) to simulate node loss, confirming the queue re-elected a leader and remained readable, then consuming all 3 messages from node2 while node1 was down. Restored node1 and confirmed full 3-node cluster health with no partitions. Completed the mandatory sequential OS-level reboot protocol on all three nodes (one at a time, preserving quorum), confirming boot-id changes on each (node1 ef457a88→f2238af4, node2 192f6cab→8e58e40d, node3 809708f3→897e6a64) and full RabbitMQ cluster/queue recovery after each. Final end-to-end publish/consume test after all restarts succeeded.
